chapter: Dance tastes, big bands and the boat
title: Society dates in Greenwood and the Delta, with showmanship on the bandstand
summary: DeDroit describes playing Dixieland for society people in Greenwood, Mississippi, trombone gimmicks, silk suits and advice on being polite.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: ever been there? And you're always playing Dixieland

for those things. Played Dixieland? We'd take a tune on Vula Boo. You never heard of that, did you? Well they had nice changes. What does it go? Bo La Bo? Bo La Bo. Oh yeah. You've heard that. We'd make 50 tunes on that thing. And then we used to do a lot of gymnastics. You know trombone plays, you used to put the slide down on the floor and he'd move his head instead of moving the slide. And we'd strike poses, that didn't mean a thing. But that's what we're doing, you know? Yeah, sure. And being young guys, we'd dress, we wore silk suits with big six dollar black leather ties and they looked like a million bucks. Well they were making money, you know. You have to know what to do. I think it's 50% of what you're doing, 50% of what you know, you know? And then you've got to be kind, you've got to be polite, you can't be telling people off, you know?
